vinci.work: A head-worn camera assistant that keeps a timestamped log of the user's activities and, on a wake word, answers questions and suggests next steps.
vinci.S→M: At regular intervals the assistant writes a timestamped text description of what the camera sees, without waiting for a question.
vinci.M→A: When the user asks, the model reads this activity history together with the live video to answer and to guide the next steps.
vinci.A→S: The camera streams continuously and the assistant answers on a wake word, but no answer is said to choose what to observe next.
vinci.M→S: The activity log feeds the answers, but the paper never says stored history shapes how new video is captured or interpreted.
vinci.A→M: Memory holds descriptions of what the camera saw. Whether the assistant's own answers or plans are also stored is never described.
vinci.record: Memory keeps captions of the user's activities, but the assistant's own answers, plans and generated clips are not said to be kept.
vinci.outcome: No user reply, rating or task result about the answers is collected, and the demos are judged only by the authors.
vinci.attribution: With no outcome collected, nothing links a result back to any answer, plan or generated clip.
vinci.revision: The models were fine-tuned by the developers before release. The running assistant changes no model, prompt, rule or code.
vinci.later_use: There is no change of its own to carry forward. Continued evolution appears only as a future prospect.

vinci2.work: A streaming assistant for first-person video that builds layered memories over days and decides when to step in with help or answer recall questions.
vinci2.S→M: Each incoming clip becomes timestamped captions and keyframes, which build up summaries, a graph linking scenes and things, and image memory across the recorded days.
vinci2.M→A: Retrieved summaries, linked past episodes and rebuilt visual context go to the reasoner, which decides whether to speak and what to say.
vinci2.A→S: The reasoner asks for past evidence and re-reads stored captions and frames, but no decision is said to direct a new observation.
vinci2.M→S: New clips are captioned before they enter memory. Nothing says stored history guides how new clips are captured or read.
vinci2.A→M: Memory is built from incoming video. The paper does not say the assistant's decisions or responses are written back into it.
vinci2.record: Memory holds only material built from video. The decision to step in and the response itself are not said to be stored or logged.
vinci2.outcome: The assistant collects no user reply, rating or result. It runs on recorded video, and scores come from the authors' offline benchmark.
vinci2.attribution: Predictions are matched to ground-truth moments only for benchmark scoring, never to check or correct the assistance.
vinci2.revision: The method needs no training. Its growing summaries and graph are material built from video, not changes to its model, prompts or rules.
vinci2.later_use: With no change made by the assistant, no later run under a revised version is reported.

visionclaw2026.work: Smart glasses with a live voice assistant that passes requests to a separate agent, which keeps lasting memories, researches online and acts through connected tools.
visionclaw2026.S→M: On the user's spoken request, what the glasses see and hear is saved to lasting stores, such as hotel details, poster notes and conversation memories.
visionclaw2026.M→A: The agent pulls saved personal information, earlier session results and calendar or email context, which the assistant reports or uses to continue a task.
visionclaw2026.A→S: Before sending a message the assistant asks the user to confirm recipient and content, and delegated tasks look up needed facts before finishing.
visionclaw2026.M→S: Calendar and email memory picks a topic that the agent then researches. No stored information is shown shaping capture or interpretation directly.
visionclaw2026.A→M: Past delegated tasks, decisions and the agent's results are stored in memory and retrieved in later sessions, as with an earlier trip-planning task.
visionclaw2026.record: Delegated tasks, past decisions and the agent's execution results are kept in accumulated memory logs that users can look back through.
visionclaw2026.outcome: Each task's result comes back to the voice assistant, and users later retrieve the results of earlier tasks, such as trip planning.
visionclaw2026.attribution: Results are only relayed to the user or fetched on request. Nothing links a result to its decision to check or correct later help.
visionclaw2026.revision: Participants added skills to their own agents, memory only grows in stored content, and the paper says the model does not adapt over time.
visionclaw2026.later_use: Later weeks drew on participant-added skills and accumulated memories, not on anything the assistant itself changed.

contextagent.work: A proactive assistant tested on wearable recordings: it reads video, audio, notifications and a given user description, then decides whether to help and which tools to call.
contextagent.S→M: Annotators write a user description for each test example. Building it up from past conversations is only named as a possible extension.
contextagent.M→A: The user description clearly shapes help decisions and tool plans, but nothing says it is kept and reused across interactions.
contextagent.A→S: Planning a hike, the assistant notices the location is missing, calls GPS, then passes the city to a weather lookup before answering.
contextagent.M→S: User descriptions enter reasoning after the video and speech are read. Nothing shows stored personal information shaping how sensing is done or interpreted.
contextagent.A→M: The reasoner outputs tool plans and replies for each test example, but nothing says these are written into lasting memory.
contextagent.record: Each test example is processed on its own, and the reasoner's help scores, tool chains and replies are not said to be kept.
contextagent.outcome: No user reply, rating or effect of the help is collected. Tool results only feed the same reply, and accuracy is scored offline against labels.
contextagent.attribution: Decisions are compared with ground-truth labels only for offline scoring, and no result is linked back to check or correct help.
contextagent.revision: The only change is fine-tuning by the developers before testing, and updating the user description over time is only mentioned as a possible extension.
contextagent.later_use: With no change made by the assistant, running the developer-trained model on test data does not count as later use.

proagent.work: A wearable proactive assistant that uses stored user preferences to decide when to offer help and samples the camera more often when help may be needed.
proagent.S→M: Preferences the user states, and ones inferred from context and feedback, are saved by scenario, merging similar entries and replacing conflicting ones.
proagent.M→A: Preferences for the current scenario reach the reasoner with sensor input, which chooses between silence and help, plans tools and personalizes the reply.
proagent.A→S: When the reasoner judges help useful, the camera keeps sampling at a high rate. A no-need decision drops it back to a low rate.
proagent.M→S: Retrieved preferences enter the vision model with the raw image, and its first output describes the current scene before any help is decided.
proagent.A→M: Each delivered suggestion is stored with its context and the user's spoken feedback, and a language model turns these records into updated preferences.
proagent.record: Each interaction record keeps the time and place, the help delivered and the user's spoken feedback, building up an interaction history.
proagent.outcome: The user's spoken reaction to each delivered suggestion is saved together with that suggestion and its context.
proagent.attribution: Because feedback is stored with the suggestion and its place, a remark that bus alerts are unwanted at one stop becomes a note to stay quiet there.
proagent.revision: Feedback only adds, merges or replaces preference notes read by an unchanged model. The model's fine-tuning was done offline by the developers.
proagent.later_use: Later decisions use the updated preference notes, but no revised model, prompt or rule exists for them to run under.

aiget.work: Smart glasses that offer knowledge about what the user is looking at, chosen by a profile of the user's interests.
aiget.S→M: The interests, values and background the user selects form a stored profile that the glasses reuse across sessions.
aiget.M→A: The profile and past history steer which knowledge is generated, filtered for novelty, ranked and finally shown.
aiget.A→S: The glasses react to gaze and to questions, but the paper never says an action decides what to look at next.
aiget.M→S: The profile tells perception which places and things the user already knows.
aiget.A→M: Delivered knowledge items are kept as history, and later outputs skip topics already mentioned when the user revisits a place or thing.
aiget.record: The glasses keep a history of the knowledge they delivered and check the ten most relevant past items to avoid repeating topics.
aiget.outcome: The user can cancel or mute a suggestion, but nothing says these reactions are kept.
aiget.attribution: Cancelling only stops the current display. Nothing ties a cancellation to the item it ended or uses it to correct later help.
aiget.revision: Prompts, score cut-offs and trigger thresholds were tuned by the developers in pilot tests. Adapting the profile or rules is left to future work.
aiget.later_use: Later outputs reuse the stored history, but the way knowledge is generated stays the same.

ai4service.work: A wearable assistant organized like a computer, with input, memory, processing and output units, that reacts to commands and visual events, searches the web and remembers past sessions.
ai4service.S→M: After each interaction, the dialogue is condensed into a local record with user details, a summary, the final output, time and topic, kept for later sessions.
ai4service.M→A: A new task retrieves related past records into the model prompt, and these combine with the scene and tool results to form the reply.
ai4service.A→S: The dispatcher sets future visual triggers or asks for detailed scene descriptions, such as watching card changes in blackjack before giving advice.
ai4service.M→S: Memory feeds the final reply, but the paper never links a retrieved record to what the trigger or vision models are asked to watch.
ai4service.A→M: Every stored record includes the assistant's final output, written automatically after each interaction so later sessions can reuse it.
ai4service.record: Each interaction becomes one stored record holding user details, a dialogue summary, the assistant's final output, a timestamp and a topic tag.
ai4service.outcome: Records keep the assistant's output but no reply, rating or result about it, and user feedback is left to future work.
ai4service.attribution: Nothing links a result to the advice it concerns. When the player busts, the analysis looks ahead and never refers back to earlier recommendations.
ai4service.revision: The trigger and dispatch models were fine-tuned by the developers before deployment. While running, the assistant only writes records and changes nothing about itself.
ai4service.later_use: Later sessions only pull stored records into the prompt, and none of the three demos shows a later session.

mementoar2026.work: An AR headset that stores each spoken question about an object with its place, time and activity, and brings it back when that routine recurs.
mementoar2026.S→M: A spoken question, its answer and source, the object asked about, and the recent place and activity are saved together as a permanent memory.
mementoar2026.M→A: Matched memories decide which earlier question to bring back and where to show it, and can produce an updated answer when the routine recurs.
mementoar2026.A→S: Before showing a resurfaced memory, the headset checks the current view for the object so the display can be anchored on it.
mementoar2026.M→S: The object named in a retrieved memory is handed to an object detector, which finds it in the current view.
mementoar2026.A→M: The assistant's answer and its source are stored permanently with the user's question and the place and activity around it.
mementoar2026.record: Each answer is placed on the object it concerns and stored permanently, together with the question and its place, time and activity.
mementoar2026.outcome: The user can permanently remove a resurfaced memory, but the dismissal itself is not said to be kept as a record.
mementoar2026.attribution: Each resurfaced memory shows the place, time and activity that matched, so the user can remove that exact memory if it was a mismatch.
mementoar2026.revision: Only stored memories change, through new entries, refreshed answers and removals. Models and matching stay fixed, and the user sets how often recall happens.
mementoar2026.later_use: Later recalls reuse stored memories under the same pipeline. Adapting appears only as a participant hope and future work.

socialmind.work: Smart glasses that read speech and body language in live conversation and suggest what to say, using stored notes about the user and known partners.
socialmind.S→M: After a conversation, a language model saves details about both speakers under their identities, merging similar details and replacing contradicted ones.
socialmind.M→A: If the partner is recognized, both people's stored notes are retrieved, otherwise only the user's, and these shape the live suggestions.
socialmind.A→S: Speech and body cues are sensed on set schedules, but no suggestion is said to request an observation or follow the reply it prompts.
socialmind.M→S: The partner's face is matched on the device against stored identities to tell whether this is someone already known.
socialmind.A→M: In daily use, both speakers' utterances, body cues and the suggestions given are saved as pairs in caches that later conversations reuse.
socialmind.record: The glasses keep both speakers' utterances, nonverbal cues and their own matching suggestions as tagged pairs in lasting caches.
socialmind.outcome: No rating, adoption or partner reaction to a suggestion is kept. The only ratings come from the researchers' post-study questionnaire.
socialmind.attribution: There is no outcome to link. The cache ties each suggestion only to the partner's remark that prompted it, not to any later effect.
socialmind.revision: Only stored notes and cached pairs change. The fixed prompt, the matching threshold and the language models are never updated.
socialmind.later_use: Later conversations only reuse stored notes and cache hits under the same fixed method.

speechless2026.work: An AR assistant that lets users ask with few or no words by filling in their intent from a personal memory of past requests tied to places.
speechless2026.S→M: Asking it to remember something, or asking a question, saves the query, the answer and a sketch of scene, object, time and intent for that user.
speechless2026.M→A: Up to five past memories reach the answer step with the current question and view, so routine help works with little or no speech.
speechless2026.A→S: When a proposed answer is low in confidence, the assistant shows its reasoning and asks the user for a Yes or No before accepting it.
speechless2026.M→S: Stored memories fill in what a short or silent request leaves out, settling what the user means before any answer is written.
speechless2026.A→M: Each composed answer is stored with its question and context sketch, and low-confidence answers are stored only after the user accepts them.
speechless2026.record: Each memory joins the question, the assistant's answer and a sketch of scene, object, time, intent and location, and the store grows with the user's routines.
speechless2026.outcome: The Yes or No on a low-confidence answer only decides whether it is stored, and the verdict itself is not said to be kept.
speechless2026.attribution: Each low-confidence answer is shown with its rationale and paired with the user's Yes or No, which decides whether it enters memory.
speechless2026.revision: Saving, deleting and refreshing memories change only stored content. The pipeline and thresholds stay fixed, and learning from the user's verdicts is future work.
speechless2026.later_use: Later questions reuse stored memories through the same fixed pipeline.

m3agent.work: An agent that watches long video with audio, keeps a graph of the people and events it sees, and answers questions by searching that graph.
m3agent.S→M: Each new video and audio clip adds event and fact entries to the graph, and entries seen again gain weight.
m3agent.M→A: To answer a question, the agent searches the graph by person or clip several times, then replies from what it found.
m3agent.A→S: The answering loop only searches stored memory or replies, and the paper never describes an action asking for new video or a fresh look.
m3agent.M→S: Stored face and voice features identify who appears in each new clip, so new descriptions keep the same person identities.
m3agent.A→M: The agent's reasoning and answers stay in the current question's working context, and the paper never says they are written into the graph.
m3agent.record: The agent's search steps and answers disappear once a question is answered, and neither the graph nor any log keeps them.
m3agent.outcome: No user reply or correction about an answer is collected. Correctness judgments serve only benchmark scoring and offline training.
m3agent.attribution: Answers are tied to rewards only during the developers' offline training, never while the agent is in use.
m3agent.revision: Both models are trained by the developers before release. In use, only the memory content grows while the models stay the same.
m3agent.later_use: With nothing revised in use, every evaluation runs the same released models.

lightmemego2026.work: A phone and glasses assistant that turns everyday video and audio into event memories, then answers questions such as where an object was left.
lightmemego2026.S→M: Video and audio segments are stored, refined as transcripts arrive, and merged into long-term episodes and the user's routines, preferences and relationships.
lightmemego2026.M→A: A query router picks stored events and personal facts by time range and intent, and the answer model replies from that evidence.
lightmemego2026.A→S: The client streams video continuously and answers questions, but no answer or plan is described asking the glasses to capture something new.
lightmemego2026.M→S: Segmenting uses frame changes and timing, and memory feeds answers. Nothing says stored personal knowledge changes how new video is captured or read.
lightmemego2026.A→M: Memory holds captured observations, transcripts and extracted routines, but the paper never says the assistant's own answers are kept for later.
lightmemego2026.record: Answers are generated from retrieved evidence, but no answer or routing choice is kept in memory or in a log.
lightmemego2026.outcome: The assistant collects no reply or rating on its answers. Answer accuracy is judged offline against annotated evidence.
lightmemego2026.attribution: With no record of answers and no feedback on them, nothing links a result back to an answer.
lightmemego2026.revision: Consolidation only adds memory content. The router and answer model never change, and the authors note that memory updating lacks a principled policy.
lightmemego2026.later_use: Later questions reuse the growing memory under the same fixed router and answer model.

sensibleagent2025.work: A mixed-reality assistant prototype that offers help on its own, adapting what it asks, the question format and how the user can reply to the current context.
sensibleagent2025.S→M: The prototype sees one camera frame per trigger plus hand-set context, and the paper says it keeps no user history or long-term preferences.
sensibleagent2025.M→A: Prompts come from the current context and fixed generic examples. The paper states that no user history or preferences are used.
sensibleagent2025.A→S: Each prompt asks the user to confirm or choose, and its format decides which reply inputs are active. The choice then shapes the response.
sensibleagent2025.M→S: The paper excludes user history, so no stored personal state guides what the prototype perceives. Context values are entered by hand.
sensibleagent2025.A→M: The paper treats each proactive interaction as a separate event and keeps no history, so nothing the assistant does is stored.
sensibleagent2025.record: Each interaction stands alone and nothing is kept by the assistant. Only the experimenters log interaction times for the study.
sensibleagent2025.outcome: The user's yes, no or option choice only drives that same interaction's reply and is not kept. Study ratings belong to the researchers.
sensibleagent2025.attribution: The user's reply only approves and selects the next step within one interaction. Learning from dismissals is proposed but not built.
sensibleagent2025.revision: Developers hand-wrote the examples and trained the classifier before the study. Learning from feedback is left to future work.
sensibleagent2025.later_use: Nothing is revised, so later visits run unchanged. Repeated-activity variants in the study come from hand-set familiarity values, not learning.

egocopilot2026.work: Smart glasses that answer spoken questions and run tools such as notes, calendar and web search, using a compressed history of past events.
egocopilot2026.S→M: A growing log stores descriptions of what the user sees and their spoken questions, and memo and calendar tools save the user's notes.
egocopilot2026.M→A: Compressed summaries of the past event and question log are added to the reasoning context before the assistant answers.
egocopilot2026.A→S: For a planned task, the assistant calls visual tools, and when choices stay unclear it asks the user a targeted question before acting.
egocopilot2026.M→S: References like "this" are resolved with short-term object tracking, but the paper never says the long-term history shapes how new views are read.
egocopilot2026.A→M: The log holds scene descriptions and user questions. Tool results and clarifier replies stay in the current request, and saving the assistant's answers is not described.
egocopilot2026.record: The log keeps only scene descriptions and user questions. The assistant's own answers and tool calls are not kept, apart from vague logging of aborted calls.
egocopilot2026.outcome: Tool results and failures are used only within the current plan. Task completion and ratings come from researchers reviewing recorded logs.
egocopilot2026.attribution: After a failed tool call, the remaining calls are skipped and the partial result summarized, with no check or correction of the decision.
egocopilot2026.revision: The authors fine-tune the model offline and hand-design the tool schemas. Adapting while in use is planned future work.
egocopilot2026.later_use: Every run uses the same author-tuned model and fixed tools, so no revised version is ever used later.

pro2assist2026.work: A wearable assistant that follows a user through a how-to task with camera and motion sensors, giving step-by-step guidance at the right moments.
pro2assist2026.S→M: Confirmed steps fill a progress list that starts empty for each task. Whether it counts as lasting personal memory across interactions is not stated.
pro2assist2026.M→A: The progress list shapes when and what guidance is given, but it resets every task, so it is unclear whether it is lasting personal memory.
pro2assist2026.A→S: Head and hand motion decide which frames to sample, and the task request picks a WikiHow guide, but no action asks for a new observation.
pro2assist2026.M→S: The progress list helps read the current images within a task, but it resets per task and no longer-lived personal memory guides sensing.
pro2assist2026.A→M: The progress list holds the user's completed steps. No record of the guidance the assistant gives is described as kept.
pro2assist2026.record: Only task state is kept, the user's completed steps and a rolling prediction window. No record of triggers or delivered guidance is retained.
pro2assist2026.outcome: The running assistant collects no reply or rating on its guidance. Ratings and step labels were gathered by researchers for evaluation only.
pro2assist2026.attribution: Nothing links later evidence to a guidance decision. A consistency check only votes over recent step predictions before moving to the next step.
pro2assist2026.revision: Developers fine-tune the reasoning model offline, and each task's guide is content. Personalization across sessions is future work.
pro2assist2026.later_use: Later guidance within a task runs the same developer-trained model and only reads the updated progress list.

pro2bench2026.work: A wearable video coach for how-to tasks: a planner keeps a step plan, and a second model watches and decides when to interrupt with guidance.
pro2bench2026.S→M: The user's request sets up a step plan, and video evidence marks steps as completed, current or next. A later mid-task question uses that plan.
pro2bench2026.M→A: The stored plan tells the coach whether to stay silent or interrupt and what to say, and answers to user questions also draw on it.
pro2bench2026.A→S: The plan lists visual cues showing whether a step is done or still in progress, and plan updates set which video clips are checked later.
pro2bench2026.M→S: Stored cues for the current step tell the model what to look for in the video, and stored timestamps pick which past clips to view.
pro2bench2026.A→M: When the coach interrupts, the planner reads what it just told the user and writes a revised plan consistent with it, used for later questions.
pro2bench2026.record: On each interruption, the coach's decision and words shape the revised plan, which later questions draw on along with the conversation history.
pro2bench2026.outcome: Video evidence shows whether the current step is still in progress, is done, or whether the user has strayed from the plan.
pro2bench2026.attribution: The planner checks new video against the previous plan, then advances the step or writes a recovery plan when the user strays.
pro2bench2026.revision: Both models are trained offline by the developers. Plan updates change task content only, and learning from the planner's own runs is future work.
pro2bench2026.later_use: Later guidance only reads the updated plan, which is task content, and runs on the same trained models.

ipibench2026.work: An assistant for live video that stores the user's requests to watch for something, alerts when it appears, and answers questions in between.
ipibench2026.S→M: New watch instructions are saved as structured tasks, later instructions change or cancel them, and past interactions are kept too.
ipibench2026.M→A: Stored tasks decide when an alert fires and what it says, and answers to questions draw on past interaction history.
ipibench2026.A→S: When the agent accepts a watch task, it writes text descriptions of what to look for, and each new frame is compared with them.
ipibench2026.M→S: Stored tasks set what new frames are compared against, and past interactions help resolve vague references before the video is processed.
ipibench2026.A→M: The user's instructions are saved as tasks, but the paper never shows the agent's own decisions or replies being written back to memory.
ipibench2026.record: Memory holds the user's tasks and loosely described past interactions. The agent's own alerts, replies and gating choices are never said to be stored.
ipibench2026.outcome: No user reaction to an alert or answer is collected. Changing or cancelling a request edits the request, and scoring is offline.
ipibench2026.attribution: A gating check compares each alert with a visual change at the same moment, before delivery, so no later outcome is linked back.
ipibench2026.revision: The framework needs no training, and the authors set gating thresholds by hand for each model. Task edits change content only.
ipibench2026.later_use: Nothing is revised, so later alerts only use the updated task list.

omi2026.work: A wearable that records the user's conversations, keeps personal facts, and offers a chat assistant with tools plus app-driven proactive notifications.
omi2026.S→M: Captured transcripts are saved as the user's conversations and turned into linked personal facts.
omi2026.M→A: Stored facts and past conversations fill the prompts for notifications, and the chat retrieves the same personal context when answering.
omi2026.A→S: In agentic chat, the assistant chooses tools like calendar reads and web search to fetch fresh information before replying.
omi2026.M→S: Saved voice profiles of the owner and known people are loaded in live sessions to tell who is speaking in new audio.
omi2026.A→M: The assistant's chat replies are saved by chat session and given back as earlier messages on later turns.
omi2026.record: Each chat answer is saved with citations to its source conversations, and the last ten messages return as context for follow-ups.
omi2026.outcome: No rating, dismissal or result for an answer or notification is collected. Later chat turns are kept only as context.
omi2026.attribution: Answers only cite the conversations they came from, which shows their sources, not how they turned out.
omi2026.revision: Developers set the prompts, memory rules and model choice. Memories and voice profiles grow, but no change the assistant makes to itself is described.
omi2026.later_use: Nothing is revised, so saved messages return only as conversation context, the last ten at a time.

bee2026.work: A wearable that listens to the user's conversations and turns them into personal history, daily insights and suggested to-dos.
bee2026.S→M: Speech from the wearable becomes saved transcripts, summaries and personal facts, which the user can revisit or delete.
bee2026.M→A: Past conversations and the user's patterns shape tailored insights, suggested goals and other help.
bee2026.A→S: Listening is ambient and started by the user. The listed integrations never show an action changing what is captured or prompting a check.
bee2026.M→S: Personal history shapes insights, but the description never shows stored knowledge guiding how new audio is captured or understood.
bee2026.A→M: Suggested to-dos are kept as items the user can later find, accept or dismiss, and accepted ones join the to-do list.
bee2026.record: To-dos the assistant proposes from conversations stay as pending suggestions, and its insights about the user can be retrieved later.
bee2026.outcome: The user accepts or dismisses each suggested to-do, and accepted ones can later be marked complete.
bee2026.attribution: Accept and dismiss act on one suggestion, but no source says the response or completion is used to check or improve later suggestions.
bee2026.revision: Only a marketing line says it learns from daily patterns, which means personal content. No change to its model, prompts or rules is described.
bee2026.later_use: Nothing is revised, and the claim that it grows richer over time refers to accumulated personal content.

assistantx.work: An office robot that carries out tasks by moving around and messaging colleagues, using a lasting graph of people, items and places.
assistantx.S→M: Incoming messages and what the robot observes go to a reflection step that updates where items are, who owns them, and who is available.
assistantx.M→A: The stored graph of people, items and places guides planning: whom to work with, where to go and what to say.
assistantx.A→S: Previous plans and finished actions tell perception which surroundings and conversations matter for the current task.
assistantx.M→S: The lasting graph is passed to perception, which pulls out task-relevant locations, ownership and active contacts.
assistantx.A→M: Executed digital and physical actions feed reflection, which updates links in the lasting graph and people's availability.
assistantx.record: Plans, executed tasks and reflection results sit in short-term memory, reset after each instruction. The lasting graph holds relations, not what the robot did.
assistantx.outcome: Replies, location and smart-lock signals after an action are kept only in short-term memory, which is cleared after each instruction.
assistantx.attribution: After each action, reflection judges yes or no whether the result matched expectations, and its reasoning guides the next planning step.
assistantx.revision: The agents run fixed prompts on a fixed model. Reflection only writes task guidance and graph content.
assistantx.later_use: Reflection guidance only steers later steps of the same instruction and is reset afterwards.

hobbit.work: A home helper robot, tried in real homes, that learns the user's objects and places, keeps calendar reminders, and picks things up from the floor.
hobbit.S→M: Objects the user demonstrates, places the user teaches, and calendar entries become lasting knowledge of objects, locations and reminders.
hobbit.M→A: Stored place labels tell the robot where to drive, and stored reminders send it scheduled commands.
hobbit.A→S: The current task decides where the head camera points, and after a grasp the robot looks at where the object lay.
hobbit.M→S: Object appearances learned earlier let the robot recognize the same objects when it later searches for them.
hobbit.A→M: The robot checks each grasp and retries at once, but the paper never says records of its actions are kept for later.
hobbit.record: Only the field-trial log keeps the robot's actions, and it serves the researchers' analysis, not the robot's own later use.
hobbit.outcome: Grasp success and the user's replies are used at once inside the task, and the paper never says they are kept.
hobbit.attribution: After lifting an object, the robot checks whether the floor spot changed, tying success or failure to that grasp before a retry.
hobbit.revision: The robot revises nothing itself. Researchers lowered by hand how often it offered to return a favor during the trial.
hobbit.later_use: With no change made by the robot, nothing runs under one. Later trial days used the researchers' hand-adjusted rule.

strands.work: A long-running mobile robot in a care facility that uses maps and logs to plan routes and choose when and where to offer information.
strands.S→M: Robot sensor messages and people's touches on its screen are stored in a database and in models of how the place changes over time.
strands.M→A: Stored travel statistics guide route choice, and learned models of screen use decide when and where the robot offers information.
strands.A→S: Docking resets the robot's position estimate to the known dock location, and starting a route also switches on failure monitoring.
strands.M→S: The stored site map is handed to the localizer so the robot can work out where it currently is.
strands.A→M: Each time the robot drives a route segment, its travel time and success are written to the database for later models.
strands.record: Every route segment the robot drives is logged with how long it took and whether it succeeded.
strands.outcome: Travel success and duration are kept, and so are logs of people interacting with the robot's screen.
strands.attribution: Each result is tied to its route segment or map spot and time, so the robot avoids failure areas and reschedules visits.
strands.revision: The only candidate is online relearning of travel and visit statistics, which feed a planner and scheduler that never change.
strands.later_use: Later routes and visits use updated predictions under the same planner and scheduler, so no changed method is shown in use.

philia.work: A long-running assistant built on OpenClaw that remembers the user's preferences and plans physical tasks, which robots carry out through a gateway layer.
philia.S→M: Preferences the user states are saved in lasting notes, and a breakfast example later retrieves the saved preference.
philia.M→A: Retrieved preferences and named places shape the plan and the physical requests sent to the robot.
philia.A→S: The assistant's workflows ask the robot to observe the scene, interleaving those observations with physical steps and recovery.
philia.M→S: Memory helps interpret what the user wants, but the same controller also plans the task, and robot perception is never said to receive stored knowledge.
philia.A→M: Long-horizon plans, task history and earlier decisions are kept as lasting state and as dated notes of each day's interactions.
philia.record: The assistant keeps task history, plans, preferences and past decisions in long-term memory files and dated daily notes.
philia.outcome: Task results drive retries within a task but are never said to be kept. Only the team's offline training data keeps corrections.
philia.attribution: The assistant reads the status and result of each robot action and uses it to decide on retries, recovery or stopping.
philia.revision: Only the team's offline retraining of robot policies changes anything. Memory holds user facts and preferences, and no prompt, skill or rule changes.
philia.later_use: Robot policies are only said to keep improving, and no later run under a revised method is reported.

abot-claw.work: An OpenClaw-based system that coordinates several different robots through a shared memory of places, objects and views, with a critic scoring task progress.
abot-claw.S→M: Detections and key frames from the connected robots fill a lasting shared memory of objects, views and places.
abot-claw.M→A: Retrieved object positions and each robot's last known location guide navigation, grasping and which robot takes over a task.
abot-claw.A→S: A generated search program moves the robot's viewpoint and repeats detection, and the task instruction tells the critic what progress to judge.
abot-claw.M→S: Memory supplies targets for planning and robot control, but the paper never shows stored knowledge shaping what the robots perceive.
abot-claw.A→M: Execution traces with critic scores are kept as structured experience, and successful runs are written back to memory.
abot-claw.record: Execution traces are logged together with the critic's scores, and successful executions are saved to memory.
abot-claw.outcome: A reward model scores progress from the task instruction and the current view, and these scores are logged with each trace.
abot-claw.attribution: When the score stalls or drops, or a grasp fails, the system treats the current strategy as the cause and replans.
abot-claw.revision: Logged experience is stored information, replanning lasts one task, and the claimed self-evolution is never demonstrated.
abot-claw.later_use: No demonstration shows a later task using the logged experience, so later use stays a design claim.

movecare.work: A robot and smart home for older adults living alone, where a cloud Virtual Caregiver decides which reminders and checks to deliver and when.
movecare.S→M: Smart-scale weights, home sensor events and smart-object data go into a central database that periodic modules read.
movecare.M→A: Stored history decides interventions, such as a weekly weight reminder sent only if no weight was recorded that week.
movecare.A→S: An unusual weight reading makes the system ask the user to weigh again, and a detected call for help sends the robot to confirm.
movecare.M→S: Each new weight is checked against the last one, flagging changes over 2%, and motion and door sensors are read against a labeled apartment map.
movecare.A→M: Results of the robot's confirmation visit are kept: unconfirmed calls for help are archived as false alarms, confirmed ones go into the caregiver report.
movecare.record: Calls for help are archived as false or true alarms, and the week's key events are emailed in a report for caregivers.
movecare.outcome: When the robot asks whether the user needs help, the answer decides whether the call is archived as a false alarm. Pilot users tried it and said 'no thank you'.
movecare.attribution: Each answer is tied to its call for help and decides whether to archive it or phone the caregiver.
movecare.revision: Developers changed the software, microphones and the robot's night-motion rule between pilot rounds, and clinicians approved the rules. The system revises nothing itself.
movecare.later_use: The second pilot round ran on software the developers had revised, so no change made by the system is shown in later use.

elliq.work: A commercial tabletop companion that starts conversations and suggests activities, personalized by a profile it keeps of the user.
elliq.S→M: Facts and preferences from conversation are sorted into a user profile, along with onboarding answers and health entries.
elliq.M→A: The stored profile, interests and earlier preferences shape when ElliQ reaches out and which activities it suggests.
elliq.A→S: When ElliQ checks in on its own, it opens a short listening window that closes if the user does not answer.
elliq.M→S: Suggestions draw on memory, but the sources never say stored knowledge changes how ElliQ listens, which sensors it uses, or how it reads them.
elliq.A→M: Usage data and profile updates from conversation are described, but nothing says ElliQ keeps records of its own actions in memory.
elliq.record: Only generic usage data for research and product improvement is mentioned, and nothing shows ElliQ keeping records of its own suggestions or check-ins.
elliq.outcome: No source reports kept evidence of how its suggestions or reminders turned out, only a 30-day program survey and beta feedback.
elliq.attribution: No source links a reply, rating or later result to the particular suggestion or check-in that prompted it.
elliq.revision: All changes come from the company: beta-test tuning, software updates every three to four weeks, and prompting by its character team.
elliq.later_use: ElliQ makes no change of its own, so none is used later. Launch tuning and software updates are developer releases.

pask2026.work: An assistant that detects user needs from a continuous input stream and answers with long-term memory of the user, tidied after each session.
pask2026.S→M: After each session, user traits and episode summaries are reconciled, decayed or merged, then saved to long-term memory.
pask2026.M→A: The stable user profile goes into the system prompt, and retrieved past episodes help decide the reply or whether to stay silent.
pask2026.A→S: Tool use and feedback are named, but no action is shown asking a question or requesting a new observation.
pask2026.M→S: The paper says memory gives observations context, but the concrete path returns memory to the reply decision, not to a separate perception step.
pask2026.A→M: Memory keeps past request histories, but the paper never says the assistant's own replies or tool choices are saved there.
pask2026.record: Long-term memory stores the user's inputs, observations and times, never the assistant's own decisions or replies. Working memory ends with the session.
pask2026.outcome: No reply, acceptance, dismissal or rating of an intervention is kept. The 1 to 5 ratings and quiz scores are study measurements.
pask2026.attribution: No deployed result is linked to the intervention it concerns. Per-output scoring exists only in the developers' offline training.
pask2026.revision: The claimed self-evolution only decays and merges stored user traits, and model training is run offline by the developers.
pask2026.later_use: Later sessions only reuse updated memory about the user, so no revised method is shown in use.

userascode2026.work: A conversational assistant that stores what it learns about the user as typed code, so it can recall facts, compute totals and raise alerts unasked.
userascode2026.S→M: Facts pulled from each conversation are appended to indexes and archives, then periodically rebuilt into a versioned code project describing the user.
userascode2026.M→A: Typed user state, retrieved facts and a list of active alerts enter later answers, so stored information also triggers unasked warnings.
userascode2026.A→S: A generate, verify and review loop runs Python checks on stored state, but no action asks the user or the world for new information.
userascode2026.M→S: Routing and lookup pick stored content for answers and checks, but nothing uses stored state to gather or interpret a new observation.
userascode2026.A→M: Dialogue archives and saved checks exist, but the paper never says the assistant's own answers are written to memory.
userascode2026.record: No log of the assistant's own answers or delivered alerts is kept. The archive holds input dialogues and the alert list is overwritten.
userascode2026.outcome: No user reply, rating, correction or effect of an answer or alert is captured. The review step only reads sandbox results.
userascode2026.attribution: Nothing from outside is linked to an answer or alert. The assistant judges a check useful from its own sandbox review, and learning which checks to keep is future work.
userascode2026.revision: The assistant's coding agent writes Python checks over user state, tests them in a sandbox, and saves useful ones as permanent alert rules.
userascode2026.later_use: A saved rule fires as soon as the state changes, and its alert appears at the start of the next session before the user asks.

lunchnow2025.work: A Slack coaching bot that helps workers plan their day each morning and reflect on it each evening, studied over 14 days.
lunchnow2025.S→M: Plans the user gives in the morning chat are stored with the day's conversations and kept for the separate evening chat.
lunchnow2025.M→A: The evening prompt includes the whole morning conversation, so the bot's questions build on that day's plan.
lunchnow2025.A→S: Evening questions ask whether planned activities happened and why, and the user's replies supply that information.
lunchnow2025.M→S: The stored plan shapes the evening questions that gather reports, but the paper never shows it feeding the intake of replies directly.
lunchnow2025.A→M: The bot's own coaching messages are stored with each day's conversation, and the full morning chat is passed to the evening session.
lunchnow2025.record: Daily conversations, including the bot's own messages, are stored in a database and the morning chat is handed to the evening prompt.
lunchnow2025.outcome: In the evening the user reports what actually happened, for example confirming they took breathing breaks between meetings.
lunchnow2025.attribution: Each evening question refers to the morning plan, so the answer is tied to that plan, and the bot follows up on it.
lunchnow2025.revision: Goals are fixed or drawn at random from a developer-written list, developers set the rules, and adaptive goals are only recommended.
lunchnow2025.later_use: Each morning starts from the same fixed prompt and nothing is remembered beyond one day, so no revised method runs later.

ouroboros2026.work: A persistent agent runtime, run live as an agent called Hope, that turns its own faults and people's feedback into reviewed fixes to its code.
ouroboros2026.S→M: Messages from several channels enter an ordered log and per-person digests, with projects and history kept for later conversations.
ouroboros2026.M→A: Stored identity, project and per-person context shape task behavior across sessions, within limits set by its constitution and owner permissions.
ouroboros2026.A→S: Task actions are checked by verification commands run on the host, and candidate fixes are inspected and reviewed before adoption.
ouroboros2026.M→S: Personal and project context is reused later, but nothing names a stored item that picks what to observe or changes how an observation is read.
ouroboros2026.A→M: Task runs, reflection, review blockers and feedback are saved as lasting error types and proposed fixes, and project journals keep the work context.
ouroboros2026.record: Each task's result is recorded on execution, objective, review and artifact axes, with verification receipts tied to code versions.
ouroboros2026.outcome: People point out problems in conversation, for example that the agent sometimes sent the same message twice, and these join its improvement backlog.
ouroboros2026.attribution: The agent traces the double messages to a duplicate-send path, and recurring failures become rows with a count, root cause and fix.
ouroboros2026.revision: The agent lands reviewed code changes itself, such as a guard against duplicate messages and a new way of assembling review context.
ouroboros2026.later_use: The reviewed fixes stay in the runtime, so later tasks run under the changed code, as the two reported cases show.

visualclaw2026-claude-code.work: A computer-workspace agent run on Claude Code that works through staged scenarios with video frames and files, and writes new skills from its failures.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.S→M: Correctly answered examples and failed attempts from each scenario are saved, building up scenario context and a bank of skills.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.M→A: Saved scenario context and retrieved skills are added to the agent's prompt, shaping its later answers and file edits.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.A→S: Inside its tool loop, the agent chooses which files and images to read and runs checks before it stops.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.M→S: Saved skills steer what the agent chooses to read, but the frame filter uses only frame similarity, with no direct memory input.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.A→M: The agent's answers and its failed workspace attempts go back into the stores of examples and skills.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.record: Correct answers are saved as examples, and each failed question with its answer and context joins a list of failures.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.outcome: An outside evaluator checks the final workspace or parses the answer, and each failure is sent back into the learning loop.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.attribution: Each failure is stored with its own question and answer, and a language model studies these failed attempts to propose skills.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.revision: After a set number of failures, a language model writes new skill cards with steps and pitfalls into the skill bank.
visualclaw2026-claude-code.later_use: Later steps run with the evolved skills in the prompt and score higher than the same agent without self-evolution.

luproactiveagent2024.work: An assistant in a simulated environment that watches a user's activity events, proposes tasks that might help, and carries out the accepted ones.
luproactiveagent2024.S→M: Each new activity event is added to memory and combined with past events and earlier conversations with the user.
luproactiveagent2024.M→A: Past events, conversations and user traits shape which task the agent proposes, or whether it stays silent.
luproactiveagent2024.A→S: While carrying out an accepted task, each action makes the environment report a new event that the agent reads before its next step.
luproactiveagent2024.M→S: Memory shapes which task is proposed, and that task then produces new observations, but no direct memory input to sensing is shown.
luproactiveagent2024.A→M: Proposed tasks are raised as new events, but the paper never says the agent's own actions are kept in memory.
luproactiveagent2024.record: The environment logs simulated user activity, the agent's proposed tasks and the user's responses to them as a stream of events.
luproactiveagent2024.outcome: Each action the agent takes makes the environment produce a new event, which the agent adds to its memory.
luproactiveagent2024.attribution: Accepting or rejecting only decides whether a task runs, and no result is traced back to check or correct the prediction.
luproactiveagent2024.revision: Nothing in the agent changes while it runs. Model weights change only when the developers fine-tune them offline.
luproactiveagent2024.later_use: There is no change made by the agent itself to run under, and the better test scores come from offline training.

pahf2026.work: A simulated assistant for household choices and online shopping that asks before acting when unsure and saves the user's corrections as preference notes.
pahf2026.S→M: The user's answers to questions and feedback after mistakes are summarized into per-user notes saved on disk for later tasks.
pahf2026.M→A: Stored preference notes are added before the assistant decides whether to ask a question and which option to choose.
pahf2026.A→S: When stored preferences leave a task unclear, the assistant asks the user a targeted question and gets the answer before acting.
pahf2026.M→S: Stored preferences decide whether to ask a question, which then gathers new facts, but nothing shows memory shaping perception directly.
pahf2026.A→M: When a chosen option is wrong, the action and the user's correction go to an updater that adds or overwrites a preference note.
pahf2026.record: Memory holds only short preference notes. The assistant's past actions are not kept as a log for later use.
pahf2026.outcome: After the user sees the result, their feedback is checked for useful preferences and saved as a note on disk.
pahf2026.attribution: Feedback comes only after a wrong choice and names the exact feature at fault, so it is tied to that action.
pahf2026.revision: Only preference notes change, for example coke to sprite. The model, prompts and pipeline stay the same.
pahf2026.later_use: Later test phases reuse the updated notes under the same unchanged assistant, so no revised way of working is carried forward.

awarellm2026.work: A workplace assistant that combines body signals such as heart activity and pupil size with visual context and chat to offer timely help.
awarellm2026.S→M: Preferences the user sets are saved in the system prompt, and the last five user messages are kept for later reasoning.
awarellm2026.M→A: Saved preferences and chat history shape what help is offered, its tone and timing, and do-not-disturb settings filter it.
awarellm2026.A→S: Sensors capture on a fixed schedule, and nothing says an offered piece of help changes what the system looks at next.
awarellm2026.M→S: Recent user messages help the system judge how far the task has progressed while it reads new sensor summaries.
awarellm2026.A→M: A short rolling summary may mention the last intervention, but nothing shows it is kept as lasting memory.
awarellm2026.record: Only a one-minute summary notes a recent suggestion to avoid repeats, and all data are deleted after use.
awarellm2026.outcome: Sensing is not used to check whether help worked, and dismissals are not captured. Ratings are collected by the researchers.
awarellm2026.attribution: No outcome is tied to a specific intervention. The note about a prior intervention only stops repeated suggestions.
awarellm2026.revision: The system changes no model, prompt or rule by itself. Preferences come from the user's survey before the study.
awarellm2026.later_use: There is no self-made change to carry forward, and the single-session study leaves use over days or weeks to future work.

proact2026.work: A chat assistant that uses idle time between conversations to predict the user's coming needs and prepare grounded notes for them in advance.
proact2026.S→M: After each conversation turn, the assistant updates user attributes, running summaries and facts, and stores prepared material for later.
proact2026.M→A: Stored profiles, open goals and prepared material decide which needs to prepare for and whether to push, queue or store results.
proact2026.A→S: Each predicted need comes with a search plan, split into subquestions that guide what evidence the assistant looks up.
proact2026.M→S: Before searching, the assistant checks how much memory already covers, then skips the search, narrows it to gaps, or searches repeatedly.
proact2026.A→M: Each prepared note, with the need it serves and links to its sources, is written back into memory for later reuse.
proact2026.record: Each prepared note is stored with the need it supports and links to the remembered or retrieved evidence behind it.
proact2026.outcome: The assistant never learns how its pushed or stored notes fared and relies on a predicted value score instead.
proact2026.attribution: Source links tie each note only to the evidence it was built from, not to any later result.
proact2026.revision: Prompts, thresholds and weights are fixed defaults. What changes at runtime is only memory content such as profiles and notes.
proact2026.later_use: Later predictions and answers reuse stored notes, but that is reused content, not a changed way of working.

longtermtoa2026.work: A chat assistant that keeps track of a user's tasks through long quiet periods and follows up when watched conditions are met.
longtermtoa2026.S→M: The user's needs and later changes of mind update task fields, and reminders are saved with conditions, status and last contact time.
longtermtoa2026.M→A: Saved constraints and task context guide lookups, reminder updates, and the choice between following up and staying silent.
longtermtoa2026.A→S: Lookup actions request current outside information, and setting a reminder tells a background monitor which changes to watch for.
longtermtoa2026.M→S: The monitor uses saved reminder conditions as filters, so stored intent decides which outside changes reach the assistant.
longtermtoa2026.A→M: Setting a reminder creates a saved task, and later progress, completion or failure updates its stored status.
longtermtoa2026.record: Each reminder is stored as a task with the username, trigger conditions, status and last interaction time.
longtermtoa2026.outcome: The task status becomes completed when the user says the need is met, or failed when the user refuses or cancels.
longtermtoa2026.attribution: The user's reply to a specific follow-up message sets that task's status, so the result is tied to that follow-up.
longtermtoa2026.revision: Only task content such as conditions and status changes. The model was fine-tuned offline by the developers.
longtermtoa2026.later_use: Later monitor checks use updated trigger conditions, which is task content, not a change the assistant made to itself.

propersim.work: A home assistant in simulation that suggests things to a simulated user based on what they are doing, and learns from the user's ratings each day.
propersim.S→M: Each user action and the assistant's matching suggestion enter a history, with recent pairs kept in detail and older ones summarized.
propersim.M→A: The day's summary and the five most similar past pairs guide what to suggest, or whether to suggest nothing.
propersim.A→S: Suggestions come on a fixed schedule from given user actions, and nothing says the assistant asks to observe or checks anything afterwards.
propersim.M→S: Stored history feeds only the suggestion step, and nothing shows it shaping how the user's actions are observed.
propersim.A→M: The assistant's own suggestions are stored with the user's actions, and scored candidate replies also go into a training buffer.
propersim.record: Each user action is stored with the assistant's suggestion, and chosen and rejected replies are kept in a training buffer.
propersim.outcome: A simulated user rates each candidate suggestion on how well it fits their preferences and context.
propersim.attribution: Ratings turn candidates for the same user action into chosen and rejected pairs, stored with that action and the assistant's state.
propersim.revision: At the end of each simulated day, the ratings train the model.
propersim.later_use: From the second day on, the trained assistant scores higher while recommending less often.

chatgptdots2026.work: An always-on ChatGPT assistant with its own cloud computer that keeps notes, picks when to follow up, and checks tasks it hands off.
chatgptdots2026.S→M: Decisions and priorities the user shares, plus findings from permitted background research, go into the assistant's saved notes.
chatgptdots2026.M→A: Saved notes and ChatGPT memory supply preferences, decisions and ongoing work to the assistant's research, documents and follow-ups.
chatgptdots2026.A→S: For tasks it hands off, the assistant reads back their results and sends follow-up instructions.
chatgptdots2026.M→S: Background research reads new findings against earlier work, for example flagging a decision that conflicts with a draft shared last week.
chatgptdots2026.A→M: The assistant keeps notes on its ongoing work, and the progress and results of its handed-off tasks stay in Activity.
chatgptdots2026.record: The assistant keeps notes on its ongoing work, and each handed-off task can be opened to see progress and results.
chatgptdots2026.outcome: Results of the tasks the assistant created are collected and kept in Activity.
chatgptdots2026.attribution: Each result is checked against the task the assistant created, and it sends follow-up instructions to that task.
chatgptdots2026.revision: Notes hold preferences and task state, and rules are written by the user. The pages describe no change to the assistant itself.
chatgptdots2026.later_use: With no self-made change described, the pages show nothing that later runs under one.

metamuse2026.work: Meta's personal assistant with a virtual machine for each user, where it keeps memory files and goals and runs background tasks with permission checks.
metamuse2026.S→M: Personal facts from chats and editable memory files are kept across conversations on the user's backed-up virtual machine.
metamuse2026.M→A: Remembered goals and patterns guide ideas and ongoing work, and approvals the user gave limit later actions through connected apps.
metamuse2026.A→S: A browser helper reads and moves through pages to finish each task, and background work watches the sources a goal names.
metamuse2026.M→S: Stored goals steer tasks that then direct browsing, but the documents never show memory shaping what is observed directly.
metamuse2026.A→M: The Goals view keeps the assistant's plans and ongoing work, and everything it generates is stored on the virtual machine.
metamuse2026.record: An activity log shows everything the assistant has done and plans to do, and the files it generates are stored.
metamuse2026.outcome: Nothing says the assistant keeps evidence of how its actions turned out. Approval prompts come before actions run.
metamuse2026.attribution: Permission answers are tied to a pending action, but that is consent before acting, not a result.
metamuse2026.revision: Claims that it builds its own tools and edits itself name no specific lasting change, and model training is done by Meta.
metamuse2026.later_use: No source shows later tasks running under a change the assistant made. Meta's promise of a better agent refers to models Meta trains.

langchaineai2025.work: Open-source email assistant code that checks the inbox on a schedule, sorts emails, drafts replies and learns from the user's edits.
langchaineai2025.S→M: The user's answers to its questions and stated email preferences pass through a reflection step and are saved in a lasting store.
langchaineai2025.M→A: Drafting reads stored scheduling, reply and background preferences, and sorting retrieves past labelled emails as examples.
langchaineai2025.A→S: Before drafting, the assistant asks the user for missing recipient or task details and resumes drafting with the answer.
langchaineai2025.M→S: Stored examples and preferences feed sorting and drafting, which may then ask questions, but no direct memory input to reading email is shown.
langchaineai2025.A→M: The original draft and the user's edit go to reflection, which writes updated preference notes and labelled examples to the store.
langchaineai2025.record: The assistant's own draft is saved in the run state between steps and handed to reflection with the full trajectory.
langchaineai2025.outcome: The user can accept, ignore, edit or comment on each draft, and the edited text or ignore label is saved.
langchaineai2025.attribution: Each correction is paired with the original draft for that email, and free-text feedback is tied to the specific tool call.
langchaineai2025.revision: A reflection model rewrites the reply, scheduling and tone instructions in the drafting prompts and stores the new prompt.
langchaineai2025.later_use: The code would read the rewritten prompt next time, but no source shows a later draft made under it.
